editorial.headline: Household and Garden Equipment Repair: Open Nationally, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans the repair and upkeep of household appliances and home-and-garden equipment, open nationally to all business scales but blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this activity for PMA in Bali today. That is the decisive local position, even though the activity is nationally open to foreign investment with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The distinction matters because the national opening does not displace Bali’s island-wide moratorium: at the large-business scale, every scope is assessed in OSS as Low or Medium-Low risk, placing this activity within the category blocked for PMA registration in the province.

The work itself is practical, broad and firmly rooted in the maintenance economy of everyday life. It covers repair and servicing for household equipment including refrigerators, stoves, washing machines, clothes dryers, air conditioners, electric irons, vacuum cleaners and other electrical household goods. It also includes the repair and maintenance of home-and-garden equipment: lawn mowers, edgers, snow and leaf sweepers, trimmers and related equipment. In clear terms, this is the business of restoring the machines and appliances that keep homes and gardens functioning.

The activity is open to Micro, Small, Medium and Large businesses. That range gives the classification room to accommodate a compact repair operation as well as a larger service business, without changing the basic nature of the registered activity: repair and maintenance of household and home-and-garden equipment. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, under the cited presidential regulations, and the recorded foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. For a foreign-owned structure outside Bali, the national record therefore presents a fully open ownership position.

Bali requires a separate reading. Its status is Blocked (risk class) because the relevant OSS risk assessment at the Large scale is Low or Medium-Low across every scope, and Bali’s permanent, province-wide moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The moratorium was identified in the record in May 2026 and is sourced to the Governor’s letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. The practical conclusion is narrow but important: national openness remains real, while PMA registration for this particular activity is blocked in Bali under the stated moratorium.
